Yeah. And it's also if you're if you're really desperate and you can't remember my name and how to get there, then Epilepsy Action, who I'm working with, they've been very supportive, actually. And they've got the survey advertised on their research page as well. So you can always go in through Epilepsy Action's research page and they have it advertised to. Wonderful. So that's the way to do it. (1:34:12)

Wonderful, because funnily enough, Myron's just made a comment from America. No doctor has ever explained my experiences. I just have them. Sorry about that. And it's true, isn't it? You know, it's the trying to compartmentalize the extraordinary. Yeah. And that's not. It's not my desire. My desire is to say, aren't we aren't we wonderful? Don't we all have access to something amazing? And and shouldn't that be honored? Absolutely. Is there anything that we've missed that you think from our conversation that you'd like to mention now or anything or, you know, do you feel? Oh, goodness me, no. (1:34:50)

I think we've spoken about so much and I could talk forever about this stuff. I don't know about you, but it's so it's it's and and the crossover, I think, with different conditions. People are always asking me, I have schizophrenia. Do you think it's like this? I think, you know, people who are non neurotypical have a different way of engaging. Sarah, have you got any final points? I also think neurotypical is a bit of a misnomer, really, because everyone's like an individual fingerprint and we're bound to be the same neurologically as we are fingerprint wise as well. (1:35:33)

So I don't think this idea of being neurotypical holds that much water. And actually, you know, we've said it before so many times on this show in terms of especially neuroscience, the materialist reductionist view of neuroscience as being that the character of a person, the emotional state of a person, the psychology of a person can be determined by just looking at that brain is not even scientific anyway. (1:35:56)

And so if we're getting to a point in science where we're recognising the interconnectedness of species, let's say through mycelial networks, then I think we're going to start to understand that human beings have a similar, perhaps not yet visible or well understood mycelial network themselves and that we're all interconnected. (1:36:15)

And that's actually a much more scientific way to look at life on this planet. And this also means that we can, like you say, honour those kinds of experiences as being perhaps sometimes overwhelming, uncomfortable and unpleasant experiences of too much information coming in simultaneously where someone can't function. And therefore, you know, I have friends that have a lot of issues whereby they experience really scary psychotic breaks and this kind of stuff. And I don't think you want to downplay that in terms of and also the same sort of delusions of grandeur and Jesus complex and this kind of stuff. (1:36:51)

Like, I think everything needs to be looked at on an individual basis, bearing in mind that we're all connected at the same time, so that the understanding that we're part of this interconnected cosmos can inform and educate the experience of an individual and that the reality of us all being interconnected is modulated through an individual's understanding and perception of the world. (1:37:17)

So it's fed by the culture of that person as they grow up and that changes the way they view these anomalous experiences, I think, quite often. But I do think, you know, it's interesting that you brought up Zikiku because I study ancient dreaming cultures and Zikiku means ghost or spirit in Sumerian and it relates to a book of dream omens, a series of dream omens, the Ishkar Zikiku. And in Babylonia, you wouldn't just have a physical physician doctor, you'd also have an Ashiku, a spirit doctor. (1:37:51)

So there's always been an awareness of spirit and if we were to return to a culture where we acknowledged that human beings even have a spirit and that we're part of a divine conscious cosmos, then we wouldn't have these problems in the first place. Culture is sick and the world is sick and society is sick and I think we'd probably find there'd be a lot less sick individuals if our culture and our society wasn't so sick. (1:38:19)

Well said. Well said, Sarah. Very impressive. That's good. Right, okay, very much. Thanks everybody for listening in. As usual, this has been recorded and it will go up as a recording tomorrow and then it will be up there for permanent viewing. So if anybody wants to watch this again, and I'm sure many people will, you have the opportunity there. Also, if you can share it with as many people as you possibly can, because this is Louise's work is incredibly important, as we've tried to stress, and it's important that we get this out there as well. Just let everybody know that at the moment our next guest will be on the 13th of August and we've got Rizwan Virk joining us from California, which means that we'll be going out slightly later. (1:39:02)

So we'll probably go out around about eight o'clock UK time and he'll be joining us from there. And this is going to be a fascinating discussion on the latest research in terms of the true nature of reality and everything else as well. So if you can join us for that, that would be really wonderful. (1:39:18)

So everybody, thanks very much again and we'll speak to you soon. Okay, thanks very much and goodbye again. And my thanks again to Sarah and thanks again to Louise for a wonderful discussion. Bye. (1:39:26)

(2024-12-05)

entry.title: 「途中で途切れた Bigfoot の足跡」の謎を解く （途中1）
entry.content:
前置き​

Ryan Burns は Skinwalker ranch の南側に隣接した土地を購入して所有しており、"Space Wolf Reserch" と名付けている。

その所有地で起きた「途中で途切れた Bigfoot の足跡」の事件を取り上げ、その謎を解く(*1)。

これまでも「途中で途切れた Bigfoot の足跡」について多数の報告があり、証拠の 写真/動画 のデータも提示されてきた。それらのデータから「Bigfoot が portal（異次元空間ゲート） の類を通って 別次元/別空間 へ移動したのだ」…的な解釈が横行している。

だが、今回の動画で提示されている状況証拠から全く別の合理的な機序があることに気付いた。この動画撮影者を含め、誰一人としてこの機序に気づいていない筈（DoD や情報機関の一部は気づいているかも）。

なお、ここでは

敷地に設置した 4トンのコンテナが勝手に移動した ⇒ この謎を解く

という事件も起きている。

(*1)​

途中で途切れる Bigfoot の足跡の謎とその解明については、

Missing-411 や Bigfoot : 足跡が途中で途絶える現象 → 合理的に説明する （途中2） (2023-02-23)

❑ 発見される Bigfoot の足跡の殆どが一つだけで、それも 99% が右足である理由 （＋追加 1） (2023-07-19)

で取り上げたが、本記事の事例では上の過去記事の謎解きの適用はかなりの無理がある。

だが、本記事の事例は全く別の合理的な説明が可能なので、それを以下で説明する。たぶん、捏造を除けば大部分の「途中で途切れた Bigfoot の足跡」の事例では以下の機序で説明できる筈。
